title: Open Maturity Model Standard (OMMS)
description: The Open Maturity Model Standard (OMMS): a YAML syntax for defining maturity models that evaluate Bitol artifacts such as data contracts (ODCS) and data products (ODPS). A maturity model expresses policies, levels and criteria; it does not prescribe level names, level count, or specific criteria.

kind.description: The type of OMMS object. For OMMS, always `MaturityModel`.

apiVersion.description: Version of the OMMS schema used. Indicates the version of the standard, e.g., `v0.2.1`.

id.description: A unique identifier (could be a UUID) identifying this maturity model.

name.description: Name of the maturity model. Optional, but recommended for human-readable identification.

version.description: Current version of the maturity model itself (SemVer). This is independent of the OMMS `apiVersion`: a model may iterate through several of its own versions while the OMMS syntax it uses stays the same.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the maturity model. `proposed` and `draft` are works in progress, `active` is fit for evaluation, and `deprecated` and `retired` are on their way out. Models commonly turn this into a policy that caps the achievable maturity level.

description.description: Object describing the maturity model for humans: what it is for, what it does not cover, and how to apply it.

purpose.description: Intended purpose of the maturity model.

limitations.description: Known limitations, including the target standard version the criteria were designed for and what that means for artifacts on other editions.

usage.description: How to use the model: the order in which policies, levels and criteria are evaluated, and what a qualifying artifact must satisfy.

targetApplication.description: The standard this model evaluates, e.g., `ODCS` or `ODPS`.

targetApiVersion.description: Version of the target standard the criteria were written against, e.g., `v3.2.0`. Used by criteria whose threshold is the special value `latest`.

policies.description: List of policies, evaluated before any level criteria. Policies express organizational rules that override or constrain the criteria evaluation.

levels.description: List of maturity levels. Levels are cumulative: an artifact must satisfy all criteria of a level and of every lower level to qualify for it.

Tags.description: A list of tags that may be assigned to the model, a policy, a level or a criterion. Tags may be used to better categorize an element. For example, `finance`, `sensitive`, `ai-ready`.

property.description: The name of the key. Names should be in camel case—the same as if they were permanent properties in the standard.

description.description: Optional description of the custom property.

id.description: Optional unique identifier for the custom property, for stable references.

vendor.description: Identifies the vendor, provider, or external system associated with this custom property. SHOULD be a stable, lowercase identifier matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (e.g. confluent, zeenea, atlan, soda). Tools MUST preserve unknown vendor values.

CustomProperties.description: A list of key/value pairs for custom properties, using the shared Bitol structure.

id.description: Optional unique identifier for the authoritative definition, for stable references.

type.description: Type of definition for authority. See the recommended values in the documentation.

description.description: Description of the authoritative definition for humans.

AuthoritativeDefinitions.description: List of links to sources that provide more details on the maturity model: an article describing the model, a canonical URL, a glossary, or the target standard's repository. Authoritative definitions follow the same structure across the Bitol standards.

Where.description: Filter applied to the items collected by the criterion before counting them. At least one of `field`, `in` or `isNotNull` is expected.

field.description: The field of each collected item to test, e.g. `type`, `status`, `content`, or a nested path such as `team.members[].dateOut`.

in.description: The item is kept when the value of `field` is one of these values.

isNotNull.description: When `true`, the item is kept only if the value of `field` is present and not null.

Arguments.description: Parameters for the metric. The known keys are listed here; additional metric-specific parameters are permitted.

having.description: Items must have these fields present. A single field name or a list of them.

anyOf.description: Items must have at least one of these fields present.

relatesTo.description: Dependency reference. Bracket notation (`[DataContract]`, `[DataProduct]`) resolves against a linked artifact of that kind; a plain path resolves within the document being evaluated.

in.description: With `count`: count only the items whose value is in this list.

caps.description: Maps `property` values to the maximum achievable maturity level, e.g. `{ active: 5, retired: 0 }`. Used by policies to express a status cap; evaluated before all level criteria.

contractIdMustMatch.description: Property path whose value the referencing `contractId` must equal, e.g. `product.id`. Used by the self-sourcing convention.

versionMustMatch.description: Property path whose value the referencing `version` must equal, e.g. `product.version`. Used by the self-sourcing convention.

Policy.description: A rule evaluated before any level criteria. Policies express organizational decisions that override or constrain criteria evaluation — capping the maximum achievable level, enforcing conventions, or defining validation rules that apply globally.

id.description: Unique identifier. Suggested format: POL-{X}{nn}, where {X} identifies the target artifact (`C` for a contract, `P` for a product). Policy IDs are only unique within their model.

property.description: YAML property path to evaluate, e.g. `status` or `inputPorts`.

type.description: `library` means machine-evaluable, `text` means auto-pass. Default is `library`.

metric.description: Metric name, from the same vocabulary the criteria use.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the policy and its intent.

mustBe.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustNotBe.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustBeGreaterThan.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustBeGreaterOrEqualTo.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustBeLessThan.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustBeLessOrEqualTo.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustBeBetween.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustNotBeBetween.description: Threshold operator, as on a criterion.

mustBeIn.description: Threshold operator: the value must be one of these. Used with `valueOf`.

mustNotBeIn.description: Threshold operator: the value must be none of these. Used with `valueOf`.

Level.description: A step in the maturity progression. The standard does not prescribe level names, level count, or ordering conventions: each maturity model makes those decisions independently.

description.description: What this level means. This could be displayed to the end-user. Be cognizant of the verbiage.

criteria.description: List of criteria for this level. All of them must pass for an artifact to qualify for the level.

Criterion.description: A measurable check within a level: a property path, a metric (`valueOf` or `count`), optional arguments, and one threshold operator.

id.description: Unique identifier. Format: L{n}-{X}{nn}, where {n} is the level number, {X} identifies the target artifact (`C` for a contract, `P` for a product), and {nn} is a zero-padded sequence within that level.

property.description: YAML property path to evaluate. Array steps use bracket notation, e.g. `schema[].properties[].description` or `outputPorts[]`.

type.description: `library` means machine-evaluable; `text` means auto-pass — the criterion documents an expectation that an evaluator does not resolve on its own, and it scores as met. Default is `library`.

metric.description: Metric name. `valueOf` reads the value at `property` and compares it to the threshold. `count` counts the items present at `property` (the share of them with `unit: percent`). Required when `type` is `library`.

unit.description: Unit of the measured value: `rows` is a count of items, `percent` is a percentage between 0 and 100.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the criterion, and of what a passing artifact looks like.

mustBe.description: Threshold operator: exact match. The special value `latest` instructs the evaluator to resolve to the current version of the `targetApplication` standard.

mustBeGreaterThan.description: Threshold operator: strict lower bound. Accepts a version string such as `v3.1.0`, compared as a version, as well as a number.

mustBeGreaterOrEqualTo.description: Threshold operator: inclusive lower bound. Accepts a version string such as `v3.1.0`, compared as a version, as well as a number.

mustBeLessThan.description: Threshold operator: strict upper bound. Accepts a version string, as well as a number.

mustBeLessOrEqualTo.description: Threshold operator: inclusive upper bound. Accepts a version string, as well as a number.

mustBeBetween.description: Threshold operator: inclusive range [min, max]. Smallest value first.

mustNotBeBetween.description: Threshold operator: exclusive range [min, max]. Smallest value first.

mustBeIn.description: Threshold operator: the value must be one of these. Used with `valueOf`.

mustNotBeIn.description: Threshold operator: the value must be none of these. Used with `valueOf`.

allOf.description: A `library` criterion names a metric and exactly one threshold operator.
`valueOf` reads a value, not a count, so it takes no `unit`.
`mustBeIn` and `mustNotBeIn` compare a value, so they go with `valueOf`.
